phase_name: G-19R Newport Scale + Street Blockout Source of Truth

figma_figjam.reason: Not used because G-19R needed repo-contained, reusable source files with no cloud/account friction. The SVG/PNG/JSON artifact set is the compatible visual planning artifact.

tooling_used: browser research into level flow, blockout, critical path, colonial wharf/tavern context
G-19R and future source alignment validators

browser_research_sources.label: The Level Design Book - Critical Path
browser_research_sources.used_for: player start, exit, beat, and route markup discipline

browser_research_sources.label: National Park Service - Salem Maritime history
browser_research_sources.used_for: colonial port wharves, warehouses, custom house, trade waterfront logic

browser_research_sources.label: National Park Service - Annapolis
browser_research_sources.used_for: planned colonial seaport precedent and 18th-century town character

player_derived_scale.measurement_basis: Alpha bounds of the current G-4.22R player atlas, scaled by Player.gd PLAYER_VISUAL_SCALE. Collision values are read from Player.tscn CapsuleShape2D.

current_runtime_scale_audit.verdict: Current three-tile Newport roads are below the 10-15 character-width harbor/commercial target and cannot be used as proof that road scale is correct.

districts.name: Harbor / Wharf District
districts.purpose: Working edge where arrival, trade, cargo, sailors, and clues physically enter Newport.
districts.player_function: Arrival read, dock clue, visible working harbor life, optional cargo inspection, transition from boat/wharf to town street.
districts.quest_relevance: Arrival harbor beat, dock clue beat, wharf lantern rumor, manifest cargo discrepancy.
districts.landmark: Central cargo landing and warehouse doors aligned to the harborfront road.
districts.dominant_ground_treatment: Weathered planks, wet cobble, mud at cargo edges, water boundary below.

districts.name: Counting House / Clerk District
districts.purpose: Official trade-pressure node where the missing manifest becomes a concrete problem instead of a vague rumor.
districts.player_function: First official objective, records window interaction, clear central route target.
districts.quest_relevance: Missing manifest beat, first objective confirmation, return/report option.
districts.landmark: Counting House frontage and notice board visible from the main avenue.
districts.dominant_ground_treatment: Drier cobble forecourt with paper/posting board and stone threshold.

districts.name: Tavern / Inn Rumor Hub
districts.purpose: Social landmark that converts harbor facts into pre-Revolution whisper network play.
districts.player_function: Memorable west landmark, rumor hub, route choice, safe place to hear named people and motives.
districts.quest_relevance: Tavern whisper beat, two-NPC rumor beat, optional hidden clue route.
districts.landmark: Large Tavern/Inn lot at the west bend of the commercial avenue.
districts.dominant_ground_treatment: Warm cobble threshold, porch/stoop, tavern yard edge, rear gate into service lane.

districts.name: Commercial Avenue
districts.purpose: Readable shop street that ties tavern, counting house, chandlery, market, and island exit into one town spine.
districts.player_function: Human-scale movement corridor with storefronts and repeated orientation anchors.
districts.quest_relevance: Two-NPC rumor, market-route clue, guidepost to island exit.
districts.landmark: Shop row and market shed stepping toward the east exit.
districts.dominant_ground_treatment: Wide cobble/wagon street with worn pedestrian shoulders and storefront stoops.

districts.name: Rear Service Lane
districts.purpose: Back-of-house circulation for deliveries, gossip, hidden clues, and believable town operations.
districts.player_function: Secondary route that teaches the town is not a flat frontage board.
districts.quest_relevance: Hidden rumor/clue route, return/report variant, service-gate overheard lead.
districts.landmark: Rear gate between Tavern/Inn and clerk lodging.
districts.dominant_ground_treatment: Packed dirt, broken cobble, service mud, fence/yard edges.

districts.name: Residential Edge
districts.purpose: Quiet lived-in town edge that gives workers and clerks homes instead of making Newport only storefronts.
districts.player_function: Soft boundary, optional exploration, believable life beyond the quest route.
districts.landmark: Boarding house row above the rear lane.
districts.dominant_ground_treatment: Grass yards, compact footpaths, garden edges, dry dirt.

districts.name: Village-to-Island Exit
districts.purpose: Clear eastward threshold where town composition opens into island exploration.
districts.player_function: Next-step orientation and first-session pull beyond Newport.
districts.quest_relevance: Island lead beat, village exit beat.
districts.landmark: Guidepost and narrowing road beyond the market edge.
districts.dominant_ground_treatment: Cobble-to-dirt transition, shoulder grass, direction sign.

districts.name: Civic / Notice Board Node
districts.purpose: Small official public node that makes the counting-house route readable and gives the journal/objective fiction a place.
districts.player_function: First objective confirmation and route reassurance.
districts.quest_relevance: First objective beat, missing manifest beat, return/report beat.
districts.landmark: Notice board at the central avenue/cross street joint.
districts.dominant_ground_treatment: Worn cobble node, chalk/posted-paper board, compact interaction apron.

districts.name: Hidden Rumor / Clue Route
districts.purpose: Optional service cut-through that lets social stealth and dock knowledge feel spatial rather than menu-driven.
districts.player_function: Discoverable alternate path from tavern/rear lane to wharf clue.
districts.quest_relevance: Optional hidden clue beat and enriched journal state.
districts.landmark: Narrow gate between tavern yard and wharf-side cargo stack.
districts.dominant_ground_treatment: Dirt/cobble service cut-through with clear clearance and no clutter hiding path.

streets.name: Main Commercial Avenue
streets.player_purpose: Primary first-session spine from harbor arrival through tavern, counting house, shops, and island exit.
streets.ground_type: wide cobble and wagon-worn harbor street
streets.landmark_sightline: Tavern west, Counting House center, guidepost east.
streets.camera_readability_note: At gameplay zoom this road must read as a place the player is standing in, not a thin map line.

streets.name: Harborfront Road
streets.player_purpose: Southern working road where cargo moves between wharf apron and commercial lots.
streets.ground_type: wet cobble, planks at wharf edge, mud feathering
streets.landmark_sightline: Water edge and warehouse doors always visible south of the road.
streets.camera_readability_note: Camera must preserve the water/wharf edge so the player understands arrival.

streets.name: Rear Service Street
streets.player_purpose: Back-of-house service route that makes lots and daily work believable.
streets.landmark_sightline: Rear gates and residence row establish that buildings have backs.
streets.camera_readability_note: Should read narrower than the main avenue but still allow two NPC clearances.

streets.name: Central Upland Counting House Connector
streets.player_purpose: Clear uphill route from harbor work into official records and civic pressure.
streets.landmark_sightline: Counting House sits at the north end; wharf cargo remains visible behind player.
streets.camera_readability_note: Route view must show the target building and enough street width for human scale.

streets.name: West Tavern Connector
streets.player_purpose: Secondary arrival-to-tavern route with strong landmark pull.
streets.landmark_sightline: Tavern sign and porch are the vertical target.
streets.camera_readability_note: Must feel like walking uphill into a social node, not cutting between icons.

streets.name: East Market Connector
streets.player_purpose: Market and exit connector that makes the east side a district, not a dead end.
streets.landmark_sightline: Market shed and exit guidepost line the player's next move.
streets.camera_readability_note: Should show continuation out of town without swallowing the market lots.

streets.name: Dock Paths and Cargo Landings
streets.player_purpose: Work paths across cargo landings and finger piers.
streets.ground_type: planks, wet mud, rope-bounded walking lanes
streets.landmark_sightline: Warehouse and boathouse doors anchor pause points.
streets.camera_readability_note: Camera must prove wharf apron width, not hide it behind cargo scatter.

streets.name: Hidden Rumor Service Cut-through
streets.player_purpose: Optional narrow route for hidden clue discovery and overheard rumor geography.
streets.ground_type: packed dirt, broken cobble, low fence edges
streets.landmark_sightline: Tavern rear gate and cargo stack mark both ends.
streets.camera_readability_note: Narrow, but still at least 3 character widths and not clutter-blocked.

streets.name: Village-to-Island Road
streets.player_purpose: Obvious exit route that pulls the player from town into island exploration.
streets.ground_type: cobble fading to dirt and grass shoulder
streets.landmark_sightline: Guidepost and road bend visible from market edge.
streets.camera_readability_note: Exit should read as continuation, not a blank map border.

streets.name: Optional Secret / Side Path
streets.player_purpose: Subtle clue route for players following rumor-network hints.
streets.ground_type: grass/dirt footpath with sparse edge markers
streets.landmark_sightline: Back-lane fence break points toward the island road.
streets.camera_readability_note: Must remain readable as optional, not confuse the critical route.

npc_routes.work_destination: central cargo landing and west warehouse doors
npc_routes.district_role: Shows the harbor economy in motion once grounded walk sheets exist.
npc_routes.animation_movement_requirements: No static sprite may translate along this route. Use grounded idle/facing now; unlock route walking only with timestamped idle/walk/facing proof.

npc_routes.work_destination: notice board, tavern porch, wharf cargo inspection
npc_routes.district_role: Official pressure thread tying the counting house to social and harbor evidence.
npc_routes.animation_movement_requirements: Do not glide a static clerk sprite. Use idle/facing station changes only until clerk walk sheet exists.

npc_routes.work_destination: tavern porch, rear service gate, central avenue social pocket
npc_routes.district_role: Social route that makes whisper-network geography readable.
npc_routes.animation_movement_requirements: Do not glide a static patron between tavern and lane. Use stationed barks/facing until full movement proof exists.

npc_routes.work_destination: market shed, mercantile door, counting-house forecourt
npc_routes.district_role: Commercial life and alternate rumor path.
npc_routes.animation_movement_requirements: Do not glide a static shopkeeper sprite. Short route can animate only after grounded shopkeeper walk/facing proof.

npc_routes.work_destination: market connector, village-to-island road, rear service lane
npc_routes.district_role: Signals the next destination and guards against east-edge confusion.
npc_routes.animation_movement_requirements: Do not glide a static courier or sailor sprite. Station at guidepost until movement proof can show grounded step cycle.

quest_beats.objective_text: Find the Counting House above the harborfront road.
quest_beats.why_the_beat_belongs_there: The player arrives through the harbor economy; the first view must explain water, wharf, and town.

quest_beats.location: notice board at central avenue connector
quest_beats.why_the_beat_belongs_there: The board ties UI objective language to an in-world civic node.
Official trade conflict belongs in the counting house, not as loose dialogue on a random street.

quest_beats.objective_text: Inspect the cargo that was moved before dawn.
quest_beats.why_the_beat_belongs_there: Cargo evidence belongs in the working wharf where goods enter and leave town.

quest_beats.objective_text: Listen for the Third Toast rumor.
quest_beats.why_the_beat_belongs_there: The tavern is the public rumor hub, matching colonial public-house function.

quest_beats.location: main avenue between tavern and mercantile
quest_beats.objective_text: Compare the dock story with the market rumor.
quest_beats.why_the_beat_belongs_there: This makes NPC information spatial and social instead of a single railroaded speaker.

quest_beats.objective_text: Follow the east road toward the old island marker.
quest_beats.why_the_beat_belongs_there: The town geography points the player to the island before runtime reconstruction begins.

quest_beats.objective_text: Leave Newport by the old island road.
quest_beats.why_the_beat_belongs_there: The exit is a place and threshold, not an arbitrary screen edge.

quest_beats.location: rear gate to wharf service cut-through
quest_beats.objective_text: Check the back way behind the tavern.
quest_beats.why_the_beat_belongs_there: The optional clue uses service geography so the town gains depth.

quest_beats.location: Counting House notice board or tavern porch
quest_beats.objective_text: Report what you found and choose who hears it first.
quest_beats.why_the_beat_belongs_there: Return/report choices use existing town nodes, strengthening memory of Newport.

camera_viewpoints.purpose: Review the whole blockout as a town plan.
what_should_not_be_visible: tiny unreadable street lines as acceptance proof
camera_viewpoints.quality_bar: Wide review may be map-like, but it must prove one authored harbor town.
Player understands arrival and where town begins within 10 seconds.

camera_viewpoints.purpose: Show route from main avenue to counting house.
camera_viewpoints.quality_bar: Counting House is a clear destination, not a scattered icon.

camera_viewpoints.purpose: Show tavern as landmark and rumor hub.
camera_viewpoints.quality_bar: Tavern reads as memorable social hub.
Avenue feels walkable at character scale.

camera_viewpoints.purpose: Show working wharf apron and dock life.
camera_viewpoints.quality_bar: Wharf reads as working harbor, not decoration.

camera_viewpoints.purpose: Show back street and optional clue route.

camera_viewpoints.quality_bar: NPC movement remains stationed until animation is proven.

camera_viewpoints.purpose: Show east exit and island-road pull.
camera_viewpoints.quality_bar: Player knows how town continues toward the island.
Quest beats belong to visible town nodes.
No debug artifacts may be needed to understand the plan.

future_placement_governance.rule: After G-19R, all major Newport street, lot, district, wharf, NPC route, quest beat, or camera placement changes must update this source of truth and the mirrored planning artifacts before runtime placement changes can pass.
future_placement_governance.minor_tuning_allowed: Small art/collision offsets are allowed only when documented in the implementation report and when street widths, lot frontage, district boundaries, quest beats, NPC route intent, and camera viewpoints remain aligned.
future_placement_governance.g19s_requirement: G-19S must consume or validate against the G-19R source JSON and implement the approved plan without inventing a new layout.
